A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Galactic center contains a large number of massive star-forming clumps, some of which are likely to be forming the nearest super star clusters.
the BGPS Galactic center data reveal the complex interplay between the formation of stars and the evolution of the interstellar medium in the Galactic plane.
the BGPS data show that the Galactic center is the most active star-forming region in the Galaxy and that the star formation rate in the CMZ is at least as large as that of the Galactic disk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Galactic center is a rich environment for the formation of massive stars, with the most massive clumps being found in the CMZ and Bania's Clumps 1 and 2.
the 1.1 mm BGPS data are a valuable resource to study the star-formation process in the inner few hundred pc of the Galaxy.

the 1.1 mm emission is a sensitive probe of the dense gas in the inner Galaxy, and the BGPS Galactic center survey has produced a rich dataset that will enable future studies of the formation and evolution of star clusters in the inner Galaxy.
